## Summary

3.4.0 serves input schemas the Anthropic Messages API accepts on every surface, can ask a person its questions in Spanish, follows GitLab.com's move of the Orbit routes, and tightens HTTP mode's authentication budgets, its listener and the configuration it starts with.

- No tool carries `allOf`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, `not`, `if`, `then` or `else` at the root of its input schema (#1509). The Anthropic Messages API refuses a whole request whose tool list holds one, and 3.3.0 served one on several individual tools and on every meta tool in the `compact` and `full` parameter-schema modes. Each rule stays in the catalog, which `gitlab_find_action` and `gitlab://tools` read, and the handler enforces it before anything is sent.
- `GITLAB_MCP_LANGUAGE=es` (or `--language=es`) serves the texts a person reads directly in Spanish: the questions and field titles of the guided flows, the confirmation of a destructive action and the progress messages (#1577 to #1581, ADR-0027). What the model reads stays in English, and a server that sets nothing, or `en`, serves the same texts as 3.3.0.
- Orbit (#1585, #1593): GitLab.com removed five of the six REST routes the Orbit tools read on 27 and 28 October, and `orbit.status`, `orbit.schema`, `orbit.tools`, `orbit.dsl` and `orbit.graph_status` now read GitLab's GraphQL API and its Orbit MCP endpoint, under the same action IDs, tool names and parameters. Since Orbit's general availability on 29 October, GitLab.com serves a namespace's index and queries only for a top-level group with the `orbit_promo` add-on or an Orbit trial; `orbit.graph_status` publishes such a group's Orbit `access` and `trial` to a token with the Owner role there, and answers a group without access with them rather than with an error.
- HTTP mode: the authentication budgets key an IPv6 address by its /64 and bound each /48, and `unix` in `--trusted-proxies` lets a proxy on a unix socket name its callers through `--trusted-proxy-header` (#1481). The two server cards and the RFC 9728 metadata are rate-limited per client address, at 20 requests a second with a burst of 200 by default (`--discovery-rate-limit-rps`, `--discovery-rate-limit-burst`, `0` to turn it off) (#1483). A listener off loopback that serves plain HTTP warns at startup, and `GITLAB_MCP_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT_HTTP=false` (or `--allow-plaintext-http=false`) refuses one (#1561). A session refused because it is not open for the presented credential is no longer described as belonging to another credential, which was false of one that idled out or did not survive a restart (#1484).
- Configuration (#1519 to #1524): a zero means off wherever it has a meaning, through the flag and the variable alike, and `0s` reads as `0`; a value the server cannot use refuses the start on both transports instead of being replaced or ignored (see Breaking changes). A stdio server no longer reads the settings only HTTP mode has, and names any it finds set, and it now honors `GITLAB_MCP_SESSION_REVALIDATE_INTERVAL`. `--max-listen-streams` sets the listen ceiling as a flag.
- `gitlab_find_action` ranks the action a plural noun names first, so `list issues` answers `issue.list` (#1470). A string parameter GitLab checks (an email address, a URL, a commit SHA, a cron expression, a semantic version and others) declares its format or pattern, and find's example call fills it with a value of that form (#1504). Every text block of a result is annotated with the priority the output format reference documents, 0.4 for a list, 0.6 for a read and 0.8 for a write, where 3.3.0 annotated most with 0.7 (#1499).
- New parameters: client-go v3.30.0 (#1460), with `member_role_id` on the access levels of project and group protected branches (Ultimate); an `avatar` on `group.create`, `project.create`, `project.create_for_user`, `user.create`, `user.modify`, `admin.topic_create` and `admin.topic_update`, `remove_avatar` on `group.update`, `project.update` and `admin.topic_update`, and 39 more `override_params` keys on `project.import_from_file` (#1640); `hide_backlog_list` and `hide_closed_list` on `group.group_board_update` (#1510); `archived` on `project.label_list`, and `ref` on `search.commits` and `search.wiki` for a project search (#1635). The board listings name every column with a work-in-progress limit (#1512), `mr_review.changes_get` publishes its pagination (#1584), and `security_scan_profile.attach` takes the `business_logic` (GitLab 19.5) and `skillguard` (GitLab 19.6) default profiles by name (#1585).
- Fixes:
  - An inline comment or draft note on a file past the first page of a merge request's diff is no longer refused as outside the diff, and the five prompts that read a merge request's changed files say when they read only the first page (#1584, from #1517 by Nikita Turchaninov).
  - `access.approve_project` and `access.approve_group` refuse a level the project or group does not grant, where `0` used to grant Developer and another level left the request pending while it was reported as approved; every membership access level parameter offers only the levels its route accepts (#1567).
  - On the meta and dynamic surfaces, a protected environment approval rule given a count and no grantee was sent as a rule for Maintainers, and an update of a rule by its `id` moved its grantee to Maintainers; the dynamic surface also turned a top-level `required_approval_count` into such a rule. Both are now refused before a request on every surface (#1503).
  - `merge_request.cancel_auto_merge` falls back to the deprecated route when GitLab 19.5 or later answers `cancel_auto_merge` with 404, as a node can during a rolling upgrade (#1594).
  - A 405 for a project named by a path it no longer has says to retry with the project's ID, instead of reading as a refusal of the merge request, file or token the call was about (#1496).
  - `job.trace` removes the timestamp a runner writes in front of each line and joins a line the runner wrote in pieces, so `tail_lines` counts the lines the job printed (#1498).
  - The external status check create and delete name the Maintainer role on the 403 GitLab 19.5 answers a caller without it (#1463), and the safe-mode preview names both spellings that turn safe mode off (#1497).
- Release and project: the image is built on Alpine 3.24.3 (#1554), and its packages are held to Trivy's vulnerability database before anything is pushed (#1553). Every release binary is rebuilt from its tag and compared byte for byte, binaries from this release on are stamped with the full commit, and `scripts/install.sh` honors `DESTDIR` (#1557). Each release opens with a written summary (#1555), and the PyPI wheels carry PEP 740 publish attestations (#1551). The telemetry guide has a worked OpenTelemetry collector example (#1471), the repository states its governance, review standard and roadmap (#1556) and a security policy that describes what happens (#1560), and every commit is signed off under the Developer Certificate of Origin (#1562).

## Breaking changes

Configurations that started under 3.3.0 with a value the server ignored or replaced now refuse to start, naming the setting:

- A unix-socket `--http-addr` whose `--trusted-proxies` names addresses and not `unix`, which used to start with `--trusted-proxy-header` ignored, so every caller on the socket shared one budget (#1481).
- `--oauth-cache-ttl` at `0` or below, in either authentication mode, as `GITLAB_MCP_OAUTH_CACHE_TTL` already was (#1519).
- A negative `--session-timeout`, `--revalidate-interval` or `--pool-idle-timeout` (#1520).
- In HTTP mode, an upload size (`--upload-max-file-size`, `GITLAB_MCP_UPLOAD_MAX_FILE_SIZE`) that does not parse, is not positive or lies above 1 TB, as stdio already refused; on both transports, a size whose byte count does not fit in 64 bits, such as `17179869185GB` (#1524).
- With telemetry on, an identity policy the server does not know, or, with no key configured, a key rotation that does not parse or lies outside 0 to 720h (#1523).

HTTP mode's budgets are shared differently (#1481): every address of one IPv6 /64 spends one fast budget and one distinct-credential budget, as the callers behind one IPv4 NAT share an address's, and ten /64s of one /48 that had a credential refused inside `--auth-distinct-token-window` block the whole /48 for every credential the deployment does not already serve. `--auth-failure-window=0` no longer turns the distinct-credential budget off, and `GITLAB_MCP_SESSION_TIMEOUT=0` turns the idle timeout off instead of refusing the start (#1519).

The Orbit outputs no longer carry what GitLab.com stopped sending (#1585): the status's `user`, `system`, `timestamp` and `formatted_text`, and each component's `replicas` and `metrics`; the schema's `schema_version`, each domain's description and each node's incoming and outgoing edges; and the index's `formatted_text`, `last_started_at`, `last_duration_ms` and `last_error`. `response_format` on the status and the index is accepted and changes nothing, and `orbit.query` refuses a query sent as a JSON object, since GitLab.com removed the JSON query DSL on 27 October.

Withdrawn, as the versioning policy allows in a minor release for what a tool could never honor:

- `pagination`, `page_token` and `order_by` on `group.service_account_pat_list` and `project.service_account_pat_list`, whose routes answer every keyset request with 405 and read no `order_by`; `sort` takes the eight orders the routes document in place of `asc` and `desc` (#1573).
- `new_epic` on `user.notification_project_update`, which the project route does not declare (#1570).
- `repository_checksum_failed` and `wiki_checksum_failed` on `project.list`, `project.list_forks`, `project.list_user_projects`, `project.list_user_starred` and `project.list_user_contributed`, which no route reads, so a list asked for them answered every project (#1570).
- `access_level_description` on the approval rules of `environment.protected_protect`, `environment.protected_update`, `group.protected_env_protect` and `group.protected_env_update`, which no route declares (#1503).
- The `name`, `path`, `namespace_id`, `default_branch` and `lfs_enabled` keys of `override_params` on `project.import_from_file`, which the import drops (#1640).
- Below the tier GitLab needs for them, the parameters GitLab drops or refuses there (#1569, #1570):
  - Premium: on `group.update`, `file_template_project_id`, `ip_restriction_ranges`, `allowed_email_domains_list`, `prevent_forking_outside_group`, `only_allow_merge_if_pipeline_succeeds`, `allow_merge_on_skipped_pipeline` and `only_allow_merge_if_all_discussions_are_resolved`; `wiki_access_level` on `group.create` and `group.update`; `repository_storage` on `group.list` and `group.subgroups`; `approver_ids` on `merge_request.list`, `merge_request.list_global` and `merge_request.list_group`; `new_epic` on `user.notification_global_update` and `user.notification_group_update`; on `project.create` and `project.create_for_user`, `external_authorization_classification_label`, `use_custom_template`, `template_project_id`, `group_with_project_templates_id`, `mirror` and `mirror_trigger_builds`; and on `project.update`, `external_authorization_classification_label`, `allow_pipeline_trigger_approve_deployment`, `ci_restrict_pipeline_cancellation_role`, `issues_template`, `merge_requests_template`, `import_url`, `mirror`, `mirror_trigger_builds`, `mirror_user_id`, `only_mirror_protected_branches`, `mirror_overwrites_diverged_branches` and `mirror_branch_regex`.
  - Ultimate: `with_security_reports` on `group.projects`; `member_role_id` on `project.member_add`, `group.group_member_add`, `group.ldap_link_add` and `group.saml_link_add`; and `prevent_merge_without_jira_issue` on `project.update`.

Refused before a request, where GitLab refused the call or did something other than it asked (#1502, #1503, #1567):

- `group.ldap_link_add` and `group.ldap_link_delete` with both or neither of `cn` and `filter`.
- On `environment.protected_protect`, `environment.protected_update`, `group.protected_env_protect` and `group.protected_env_update`: a protect with no deploy access level, a deploy access level naming other than exactly one of `access_level`, `user_id` and `group_id`, an approval rule naming none of the three unless `_destroy` is true, an `access_level` other than 20, 30, 40 or 60, and a top-level `required_approval_count` above 0, which GitLab refuses as deprecated.
- `access.approve_project` and `access.approve_group` at a level the project or group does not grant, `0` included, which used to grant Developer.

## Upgrading

1. A unix-socket deployment that lists proxies in `--trusted-proxies` adds `unix` to the list.
2. Remove an `--oauth-cache-ttl` of `0` or below, which ran an oauth deployment at the 15-minute default and was never read in legacy mode, and turn a negative `--session-timeout`, `--revalidate-interval` or `--pool-idle-timeout` into `0`, which is what the server made of it.
3. Correct the upload size the server names at startup: in HTTP mode it ran under `2GB`, or under the 1 TB ceiling for a size above it, and on either transport a size whose byte count does not fit in 64 bits ran as a much smaller or an unlimited one.
4. With telemetry on, correct the identity policy (`none`, `pseudonymous` or `full`) or the key rotation the server names at startup; while it was wrong, the server recorded nothing about callers.
5. A listener off loopback that serves plain HTTP behind a proxy that terminates TLS sets `GITLAB_MCP_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT_HTTP=true` (or `--allow-plaintext-http`) to say so, which logs the line at INFO instead of warning. A container that keeps the image's command sets the variable, since an argument after the image name replaces the command.
6. Send `orbit.query` its query as GQL text.
7. Leave a withdrawn parameter out of a call. An imported project takes its name, path and namespace from the import's own `name`, `path` and `namespace`, and its default branch and LFS setting from a `project.update` after it; the service account token lists are ordered with one of the eight `sort` values, such as `created_desc`, rather than with `order_by` and `asc` or `desc`.
8. Approve an access request at Developer by leaving `access_level` out, rather than sending `0`.
9. Name the grantee of every protected environment approval rule (`access_level: 40` for Maintainers), which the meta and dynamic surfaces used to fill in, and send a required count as the rule's `required_approvals` rather than as a top-level `required_approval_count`.

## Security

- TODO: the advisory fixed in this release, added once it is published.
- Dependencies: Go 1.27.3 (#1455), a security release of `crypto/x509`, fixes GO-2026-6809 (CVE-2026-111943), which the 3.3.0 binaries carry, and `golang.org/x/net` v0.62.0 (#1564) fixes GO-2026-6860 and GO-2026-6866 in `x/net/html`. The image moves to Alpine 3.24.3 (#1554), which fixes CVE-2026-85091 in zlib and CVE-2026-107891 in musl, both in the 3.3.0 image.
- Hardening without an advisory, in HTTP mode:
  - An IPv6 caller that changed its address inside its /64 was given a fresh fast budget and a fresh distinct-credential budget on every request; the budgets now key the /64 and count the refused /64s of each /48 (#1481).
  - Behind `--trusted-proxy-header`, the transport-source budget kept a record of every (source, key) pair it charged, both chosen by the caller, until its five-minute sweep, including for sources its limiter never recorded; it now keeps a pair only for a failure its limiter counted, and at most 500 for one source (#1482).
